description: We are a passionate group of builders, problem-solvers, and space enthusiasts uniting for the this challenge. Inspired by the resilience and clarity of Earth’s nearest celestial neighbor, we focus on turning complex space and planetary data into intuitive, human-centered software solutions. Combining sharp engineering with clean design, We is ready to tackle real-world space exploration challenges and build tools that bridge the gap between deep-space science and everyday accessibility.
summary:
Earth’s climate is constantly shifting, but raw satellite tables and complex climate models make it difficult for students and everyday citizens to see what is actually changing in their own backyard—and whether those shifts are real trends or just normal weather swings.

**TerraSleuth** solves this by turning users into Earth System Trend Detectives. Through an interactive world map, anyone can click any location on Earth—or explore curated NASA case studies like Kochi’s warming monsoon, Amazon drying, and Arctic climate variability—to inspect multi-decade temperature, precipitation, solar radiation, and humidity records from NASA’s POWER API and MERRA-2 reanalysis datasets.

Instead of leaving users to guess at noisy graphs, TerraSleuth automatically strips away seasonal cycles using a 12-month rolling average and runs real statistical forensics, including Mann-Kendall significance tests, Sen’s slope decade rates, confidence intervals, and changepoint detection. It even lets users compare two regions side by side to see how the same global forces can push different parts of the planet in opposite directions. Finally, TerraSleuth translates the math into a clear, plain-English **Detective Verdict**, helping anyone understand what is changing, where it is happening, and why it matters.
details:
TerraSleuth is an interactive web application designed to turn students, researchers, and everyday citizens into Earth System Trend Detectives. Users can click anywhere on an interactive global map—or select from curated regional case files—to fetch 30 to 40+ years of monthly Earth science data, including 2m air temperature (T2M), precipitation (PRECTOTCORR), surface solar radiation (ALLSKY_SFC_SW_DWN), and relative humidity (RH2M).

Rather than displaying raw, noisy weather tables, TerraSleuth automatically strips out seasonal cycles using a 12-month rolling average and runs an in-browser statistical forensics engine. It computes the rate of change per decade (Sen’s slope), runs a non-parametric Mann-Kendall trend test ($S$, $Z$-score, and $p$-value), calculates 95% confidence intervals, and pinpoints the exact changepoint year where the largest historical shift occurred. It also includes a guided 3-step Investigation Wizard and a Compare Opposite Regions split-screen mode that demonstrates how the same global climate drivers can push two different regions in opposite directions.

Benefits & Intended Impact Scientific climate datasets are often locked behind complex file formats and specialized statistical software, creating a barrier for high school and college students. TerraSleuth bridges that gap by pairing accessible, plain-English variable definitions with real statistical rigor. By translating statistical significance ($p < 0.05$) into a clear Detective Verdict (Clue, Suspect, and Why It Matters), the tool empowers learners to distinguish true long-term environmental shifts from short-term natural variability—promoting scientific honesty and data literacy.

Tools, Languages, Software & NASA Resources Used

  • Languages & Libraries: HTML5, CSS3, vanilla JavaScript (ES6+), Leaflet.js (interactive mapping), and Chart.js (time-series visualization and changepoint markers).
  • Development & Hosting: Developed using Google Antigravity IDE (used as an AI coding collaborator to accelerate UI scaffolding and statistical module implementation), version-controlled on GitHub ([github.com/arjid200/TerraSleuth](https://github.com/arjid200/TerraSleuth)), and deployed as a zero-backend static web application via GitHub Pages.
  • NASA Data Resources: Live global pin-drops query the NASA POWER Temporal API (1985–2025), backed by NASA MERRA-2 assimilation data. Pre-loaded regional case files use verified 30-year monthly NASA POWER / MERRA-2 CSV datasets (1995–2024, 0.5° × 0.625° spatial resolution) alongside support for user-uploaded CSV exports from NASA Giovanni and AppEEARS (covering missions and models such as GPM, MODIS, OMI, AIRS, and GLDAS).

Creativity & Design Considerations

  • Detective Framing: Reframing statistical hypothesis testing as an environmental "crime scene investigation" makes abstract metrics like $p$-values and deseasonalization intuitive and engaging for students.
  • Scientific Honesty & Spatial Scale: Our team explicitly designed TerraSleuth to highlight non-significant trends alongside significant ones—for example, showing how high year-to-year polar variability at a single Arctic grid point (80.00°N, 0.01°E) masks long-term warming over a 30-year window, whereas Kochi, Kerala (9.93°N, 76.27°E) exhibits statistically significant warming (+0.27°C/decade, $p < 0.0001$) alongside highly variable monsoon rainfall, and the Amazon Basin (3.10°S, 60.00°W) experiences both significant warming (+0.35°C/decade) and drying (-0.52 mm/day/decade). We also explicitly note the ~50–70 km MERRA-2 grid-cell footprint so users understand spatial resolution limits.
  • Zero-Friction Accessibility: By running all statistical calculations purely client-side in JavaScript and bundling pre-verified CSV case studies locally, TerraSleuth requires zero installation, zero server overhead, and loads instantaneously even on low-bandwidth connections.
